These are conditional illustrations, not a complete issuer forecast, actual maturity schedule or accepted central underwriting case. Actual December financing/distributions demonstrate why the excluded-financing scenario cannot represent the issuer’s complete cash path. facts.label: T2H.6 — calculated metrics and definitions
facts.text: M1 = closing total carrying debt / annual model EBITDA; M2 = (closing debt minus all modeled cash) / annual model EBITDA; M3 = annual model EBITDA / modeled interest on opening debt; M4 = annual cash proxy / closing debt. These are neither covenant nor agency ratios, fixed-charge coverage nor creditor-quality earnings measures. Each denominator used for a ratio is positive. Missing minimum cash/access prevents liquidity runway in every case.

spans.text: # CP-2G
## Request

View: Under the stipulated annual paths, TDG’s carrying leverage declines, but the downside first crosses the 3x coverage watch in FY2025 and remains below it through FY2027. Positive model cash does not establish accessible liquidity. Reference closing cash initially falls to USD3043.358886m after the stipulated October distribution and repayment, then rebuilds; downside cash rebuilds much more slowly. These are conditional illustrations, not a complete issuer forecast, actual maturity schedule or accepted central underwriting case. Earnings delivery, cash conversion and capital retention dominate the result. The stronger-margin countercase improves coverage without accelerating the fixed debt repayment. Actual December financing/distributions demonstrate why the excluded-financing scenario cannot represent the issuer’s complete cash path. Only CP-2 owns the integrated credit view; no rating, probability, legal-capacity opinion or security recommendation is made.

Run `sol-remaining-tdg-forecast-20261105`; CP-2G attempt 1; execution **2026-11-05**; selected method **deploy-v-r14**; public / distressed_restructuring; owned object `forward_credit_model`. Historical opening: FY2024 flows, 2023-10-01–2024-09-30, and September 30, 2024 balances. Guidance date: **2024-11-07**. Entity: TransDigm Group Incorporated and consolidated controlled subsidiaries, including TransDigm Inc.; U.S. GAAP history, separate non-GAAP earnings and analytical model measures. Monetary quantities are **USD millions**; ratios are times or fractions as identified. No standalone financing-subsidiary or guarantor cash perimeter is constructed.

This authorized sol-medium full-method response applies all six analytical phases and nine registers. It does not claim full issuer forecasting sufficiency, native-owner acceptance or downstream publication. December 2024 is separately dated retrospective context, not a new annual opening or an as-of-November backtest. The 89/91-day current/comparative quarterly windows are not annualized. No realized FY2025 annual outcome enters any illustration.

### T2H.8 — deleveraging and disconfirmation

**Reference trajectory and dependencies.** At the annual observation points, debt declines from24880 to23880/22880/21880 only because the scenario commands1000 repayment each year. Earnings growth then reduces total leverage from FY2025 5.096956x to FY2027 4.235896x. That is arithmetic conditional on payments, not evidence that internally generated surplus will actually be swept to creditors. Cash first falls to3043.358886 and later reaches6036.608387, so mechanical net leverage improves to3.067228x by FY2027; reported cash access, minimum operating needs and actual capital allocation remain unverified. FY2025 is the lowest modeled annual-end cash point, not a demonstrated intra-year trough. No peak external funding requirement or minimum accessible liquidity can be established without dated receipts/payments and access evidence.

**Downside transmission and first inflection.** CP-2’s demand/cost chain and CP-DR E7 point first to weaker aftermarket/OEM deliveries, unfavorable mix or costs not recovered in pricing. The operating break would be orders/delivery conversion or cash-backed margins weakening; the model represents the resulting earnings loss by a fixed20% haircut every year while leaving revenue unchanged, not by claiming a separate20% sales shock. Margin becomes0.42352; interest is10% higher. EBITDA loss transmits one-for-one through modelCFO because tax/WC and capex shares do not flex. In FY2025, proxy cash is1086.30995312 below reference; after the same distribution and repayment, cash is1957.048932. Coverage2.282544x breaches the3x watch in that first year and stays below3x through FY2027 even though total leverage falls to5.294869x and proxy remains positive. Liquidity could constrain earlier within the year, but that cannot be timed here. Weak collection, retained inventory or more payouts could worsen reality beyond this fixed model. No tax shield, WC release or remedial financing benefit is assumed.

**Strongest supported counterargument and disconfirming upside.** The original growth guidance, CP-2’s installed-base economics, historical positive operating cash and financing execution, and CP-2E’s fixed coupons/documented hedges all oppose an automatic distress conclusion. The margin-only upside holds sales, capex, tax/WC, interest, repayment and distributions fixed but uses0.5494 margin. FY2025 proxy rises176.99848 above reference; FY2027 cash reaches6594.596095, coverage3.904807x and net leverage2.851479x. This case wins economically only if margins are cash-backed after recurring integration/remuneration costs, cash remains accessible, renewal/funding is documented and additional extraction does not absorb retention. It challenges the size of downside, not the missing-access qualification. It supplies no extra repayment because there is no sweep.

**Actual context changes conviction, not opening inputs.** CP-2D reports positive Q1 OCF752, yet cash falls3802 to2459 after4396 distributions and316 repurchases; financing includes163 securitization proceeds and35 option proceeds. The observed bridge is not the scenario’s4348-only allocation or excluded-financing universe. Annual October equivalent disclosure132 versus quarterly131 and October totals4348/4347 remain an unresolved1 difference; whole-quarter4396 has broader scope. The scenario retains the instructed approximate4348, rather than silently replacing it with4396 or double-deducting4216 payable. Positive operations are credible counterevidence; additional allocation and conditional access lower confidence that these paths predict issuer cash. Confidence is Medium for bounded interpretation, not a computed script score or full forecast certification.
